title_en: Tendering and Bidding Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purpose of regulating tender and bid activities, protecting national interests, public interests and the legitimate rights and interests of the parties involved in tender and bid activities, improving economic benefits, and ensuring project quality.
Article 2 Any tender and bid activities conducted within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be governed by this Law.
Article 4 No entity or individual may break up a project that must be subject to tender according to law into smaller parts or circumvent tender in any other manner.
Article 5 Tender and bid activities shall follow the principles of openness, fairness, impartiality and good faith.

Article 6 The tender and bid activities of projects that must be subject to tender according to law shall not be restricted by region or department. No entity or individual may illegally restrict or exclude legal persons or other organizations from outside the region or system from participating in bids, nor may they unlawfully interfere in tender and bid activities in any manner.

Article 7 Tender and bid activities and the parties involved shall accept supervision implemented according to law.
The relevant administrative supervision departments shall supervise tender and bid activities according to law and shall investigate and deal with illegal acts in tender and bid activities according to law.
The administrative supervision over tender and bid activities and the specific division of functions and powers among the relevant departments shall be prescribed by the State Council.
Article 8 A tenderer is a legal person or other organization that proposes a tender project and conducts tender in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 9 Where a tender project needs to undergo project approval procedures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the state, the approval procedures shall be completed and approval obtained first.
The tenderer shall have corresponding funds for the tender project or have secured the source of funds, and shall truthfully state this in the tender documents.

Article 10 Tender may be either public tender or invited tender.
Public tender refers to a tenderer inviting unspecified legal persons or other organizations to submit bids by means of a tender notice.
Invited tender refers to a tenderer inviting specific legal persons or other organizations to submit bids by means of a bid invitation letter.

Article 11 For key national projects designated by the State Council's development planning department and key local projects designated by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, where public tender is not appropriate, invited tender may be conducted with the approval of the State Council's development planning department or the people's government of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 12 A tenderer shall have the right to select a tender agency on its own and entrust it with the handling of tender matters. No entity or individual may designate a tender agency for the tenderer in any manner.
Where a tenderer has the capability to prepare tender documents and organize bid evaluation, it may handle the tender matters on its own. No entity or individual may compel it to entrust a tender agency with the handling of tender matters.
For a project that must be subject to tender according to law, where the tenderer handles the tender matters on its own, it shall file with the relevant administrative supervision department.

Article 13 A tender agency is a social intermediary organization established according to law, engaged in tender agency business and providing relevant services.
A tender agency shall satisfy the following conditions:
(1) having a business place and corresponding funds for engaging in tender agency business;
(2) having the corresponding professional capability to prepare tender documents and organize bid evaluation.
Article 14 A tender agency shall not have any subordinate relationship or other interest relationship with administrative organs or other state organs.
Article 15 A tender agency shall handle tender matters within the scope entrusted by the tenderer and shall comply with the provisions of this Law concerning tenderers.

Article 16 Where a tenderer adopts the method of public tender, it shall publish a tender notice. The tender notice for a project that must be subject to tender according to law shall be published through newspapers, information networks, or other media designated by the state.
The tender notice shall contain the name and address of the tenderer, the nature, quantity, place and time of implementation of the tender project, and the method for obtaining the tender documents.

Article 17 Where a tenderer adopts the method of invited tender, it shall send bid invitation letters to three or more specific legal persons or other organizations that have the capability to undertake the tender project and have good credit standing.
The bid invitation letter shall contain the matters specified in paragraph 2 of Article 16 of this Law.

Article 18 A tenderer may, in accordance with the requirements of the tender project itself, require potential bidders to provide relevant qualification documents and performance information in the tender notice or bid invitation letter, and conduct qualification examination of potential bidders; where the state has provisions on the qualification conditions of bidders, such provisions shall be followed.
A tenderer may not use unreasonable conditions to restrict or exclude potential bidders, nor may it grant discriminatory treatment to potential bidders.

Article 19 A tenderer shall prepare tender documents based on the characteristics and needs of the tender project. The tender documents shall include all substantive requirements and conditions such as the technical requirements of the tender project, the criteria for examining bidders' qualifications, the requirements for bid quotation, and the criteria for bid evaluation, as well as the main terms of the contract to be entered into.
Where the state has provisions on the technology and standards of the tender project, the tenderer shall propose corresponding requirements in the tender documents in accordance with such provisions.
Where the tender project needs to be divided into bid sections and the construction period determined, the tenderer shall reasonably divide the bid sections and determine the construction period, and state such information in the tender documents.
Article 20 The tender documents may not require or designate specific producers or suppliers, nor contain any other content that favors or excludes potential bidders.
Article 21 The tenderer may, based on the specific conditions of the tender project, organize potential bidders to inspect the project site.

Article 22 The tenderer shall not disclose to others the names and number of potential bidders who have obtained the tender documents, or other information relating to tenders and bids that may affect fair competition.
If the tenderer has set a bid evaluation base price, it shall be kept confidential.

Article 23 If the tenderer makes necessary clarifications or modifications to the issued tender documents, it shall notify all recipients of the tender documents in writing at least fifteen days prior to the deadline for submission of bid documents required in the tender documents. The contents of such clarifications or modifications shall form an integral part of the tender documents.

Article 24 The tenderer shall determine a reasonable period of time needed by bidders to prepare their bid documents; provided, however, that for projects that are subject to mandatory tender according to law, the shortest period from the date of issuing the tender documents to the deadline for submission of bid documents by bidders shall not be less than twenty days.

Article 25 A bidder is a legal person or other organization that responds to a tender and participates in the competition for bids.
Where a scientific research project subject to tender according to law permits individuals to participate in the bidding, such individuals shall be governed by the provisions of this Law concerning bidders.

Article 26 A bidder shall have the capability to undertake the tender project; where relevant State regulations or the tender documents impose qualification requirements on bidders, the bidder shall meet such qualification requirements.

Article 27 A bidder shall prepare its bid documents in accordance with the requirements of the tender documents. The bid documents shall respond to the substantive requirements and conditions set forth in the tender documents.
Where the tender project involves construction, the bid documents shall include the resumes and achievements of the proposed project manager and key technical personnel, as well as the machinery and equipment to be used for completing the tender project.

Article 28 A bidder shall deliver its bid documents to the bid submission place before the deadline for submission of bid documents as required by the tender documents. Upon receipt of the bid documents, the tenderer shall sign for and keep them, and shall not open them. If the number of bidders is less than three, the tenderer shall re-tender in accordance with this Law.
Bid documents delivered after the deadline for submission of bid documents as required by the tender documents shall be rejected by the tenderer.

Article 29 Before the deadline for submission of bid documents as required by the tender documents, a bidder may supplement, modify or withdraw its bid documents already submitted, and shall notify the tenderer in writing. The contents of supplements or modifications shall form an integral part of the bid documents.

Article 30 If a bidder intends, after winning the bid, to subcontract part of the non-major, non-critical work of the winning project based on the actual conditions of the project as specified in the tender documents, it shall state this in its bid documents.

Article 31 Two or more legal persons or other organizations may form a consortium and jointly bid as one bidder.
All parties to the consortium shall have the corresponding capability to undertake the tender project; where relevant State regulations or the tender documents impose qualification requirements on bidders, all parties to the consortium shall meet the corresponding qualification requirements. If the consortium consists of units of the same professional field, the qualification grade shall be determined based on the lower qualification grade among them.
All parties to the consortium shall enter into a joint bidding agreement specifying the work and responsibilities each party intends to undertake, and shall submit the joint bidding agreement together with the bid documents to the tenderer. If the consortium wins the bid, all parties to the consortium shall jointly enter into a contract with the tenderer and bear joint and several liability to the tenderer for the winning project.
The tenderer shall not force bidders to form a consortium or restrict competition among bidders.

Article 32 Bidders shall not collude with each other in bidding prices, or exclude fair competition among other bidders, thereby harming the lawful rights and interests of the tenderer or other bidders.
Bidders shall not collude with the tenderer in bidding, thereby harming the national interest, the public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others.
Bidders are prohibited from seeking a winning bid by bribing the tenderer or members of the bid evaluation committee.
Article 33 A bidder shall not submit a bid price lower than cost, nor bid in the name of another person or engage in fraud by other means to obtain a winning bid.

Article 34 Bid opening shall be conducted publicly at the same time as the deadline for submission of bid documents as specified in the tender documents; the place for bid opening shall be the place specified in advance in the tender documents.
Article 35 Bid opening shall be presided over by the tenderer, and all bidders shall be invited to participate.

Article 36 At the time of bid opening, the bidders or their elected representatives shall inspect the sealing of the bid documents, or the notarization institution entrusted by the tenderer may inspect and notarize them; after confirmation that there is no discrepancy, the staff shall open the seals publicly and read out the bidders' names, bid prices, and other main contents of the bid documents.
All bid documents received by the tenderer before the deadline for submission of bid documents as required by the tender documents shall be opened and read out publicly at the bid opening.
The bid opening process shall be recorded and the records shall be kept for reference.

Article 37 Bid evaluation shall be undertaken by a bid evaluation committee formed by the tenderer according to law.
For projects subject to mandatory tender according to law, the bid evaluation committee shall be composed of representatives of the tenderer and experts in relevant technical, economic and other fields; the number of members shall be an odd number of five or more, of which the number of experts in technical, economic and other fields shall not be less than two-thirds of the total number of members.
The experts mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall have been engaged in relevant fields for at least eight years and have senior professional titles or equivalent professional competence, and shall be determined by the tenderer from the list of experts provided by the relevant departments under the State Council or the relevant departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, or from the expert database of tender agency institutions then the list of experts in relevant specialties; for ordinary tender projects, random selection may be adopted; for special tender projects, the tenderer may directly determine the experts.
No person who has a conflict of interest with any bidder may serve on the bid evaluation committee for the relevant project; any such person already serving shall be replaced.
The list of members of the bid evaluation committee shall be kept confidential until the determination of the winning bidder.

Article 38 The tenderer shall take necessary measures to ensure that bid evaluation is conducted under strict confidentiality.
No unit or individual may unlawfully interfere with or influence the process or outcome of bid evaluation.

Article 39 The bid evaluation committee may require a bidder to make necessary clarifications or explanations regarding ambiguous contents in the bid documents; however, such clarifications or explanations shall not go beyond the scope of the bid documents or change the substantive content of the bid documents.

Article 40 The bid evaluation committee shall evaluate and compare the bid documents in accordance with the evaluation criteria and methods specified in the tender documents; if a bid evaluation base price is set, it shall be taken as reference. After completing the evaluation, the bid evaluation committee shall submit a written evaluation report to the tenderer and recommend qualified candidates for winning the bid.
The tenderer shall determine the winning bidder based on the written evaluation report submitted by the bid evaluation committee and the recommended candidates. The tenderer may also authorize the bid evaluation committee to directly determine the winning bidder.
If the State Council has special provisions regarding the evaluation of specific tender projects, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 42 Where the bid evaluation committee, after evaluation, considers that all bids do not meet the requirements of the tender documents, it may reject all bids.
Where all bids in a project for which tender is required by law are rejected, the tenderer shall conduct a new tender in accordance with this Law.
Article 43 Before determining the winning bidder, the tenderer shall not negotiate with any bidder on substantive matters such as the bid price and the bid proposal.

Article 44 Members of the bid evaluation committee shall perform their duties objectively and impartially, abide by professional ethics, and bear personal responsibility for the evaluation opinions they give.
Members of the bid evaluation committee shall not have private contacts with bidders, nor accept property or other benefits from bidders.
Members of the bid evaluation committee and relevant staff participating in the evaluation shall not disclose the evaluation and comparison of the bid documents, the recommendation of candidates for winning the bid, or other information related to the bid evaluation.

Article 45 After the winning bidder is determined, the tenderer shall issue a notice of award to the winning bidder and simultaneously notify all unsuccessful bidders of the result of the award.
The notice of award is legally binding on both the tenderer and the winning bidder. After the notice of award is issued, if the tenderer changes the result of the award, or if the winning bidder abandons the winning project, the party concerned shall bear legal liability according to law.

Article 46 The tenderer and the winning bidder shall, within thirty days from the date of issuance of the notice of award, enter into a written contract in accordance with the tender documents and the bid documents of the winning bidder. The tenderer and the winning bidder shall not conclude any other agreement that deviates from the substantive content of the contract.
Where the tender documents require the winning bidder to provide a performance bond, the winning bidder shall provide it.

Article 47 For a project for which tender is required by law, the tenderer shall, within fifteen days from the date of determining the winning bidder, submit a written report on the tender and bid situation to the relevant administrative supervisory department.

Article 48 The winning bidder shall perform its obligations in accordance with the contract and complete the winning project. The winning bidder shall not transfer the winning project to others, nor shall it break up the winning project and transfer it to others separately.
The winning bidder may, in accordance with the contract or with the consent of the tenderer, subcontract part of the non-main, non-critical work of the winning project to others for completion. The subcontractor shall have the corresponding qualifications and shall not subcontract again.
The winning bidder shall be liable to the tenderer for the subcontracted work, and the subcontractor shall bear joint and several liability for the subcontracted work.

Article 49 Where, in violation of this Law, a project that must be tendered is not tendered, or a project that must be tendered is broken down into parts or avoided by any other means, the relevant authority shall order rectification within a time limit, and may impose a fine of not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the project contract amount; for a project that uses wholly or partially state-owned funds, the project execution may be suspended or the fund allocation may be suspended; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 50 Where a tender agency, in violation of this Law, discloses information and materials related to tender and bid activities that shall be kept confidential, or colludes with the tenderer or bidders to harm the interests of the State, the public interest, or the lawful rights and interests of others, it shall be fined not less than 50,000 yuan and not more than 250,000 yuan; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be fined not less than five percent and not more than ten percent of the fine imposed on the unit; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall also be confiscated; if the circumstances are serious, the agency shall be prohibited from acting as an agent for projects for which tender is required by law for a period of one to two years and such prohibition shall be announced, and finally the business license may be revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law. If losses are caused to others, compensation liability shall be borne according to law.
Where the acts listed in the preceding paragraph affect the result of the award, the award shall be invalid.

Article 51 Where a tenderer restricts or excludes potential bidders with unreasonable conditions, gives discriminatory treatment to potential bidders, forces bidders to form a consortium to bid jointly, or restricts competition among bidders, the tenderer shall be ordered to correct, and may be fined not less than 10,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan.

Article 52 Where the tenderer of a project for which tender is required by law discloses to others the names and numbers of potential bidders who have obtained the tender documents, or other information related to tender and bid that may affect fair competition, or discloses the tender base price, the tenderer shall be given a warning, and may also be fined not less than 10,000 yuan and not more than 100,000 yuan; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Where the acts listed in the preceding paragraph affect the result of the award, the award shall be invalid.

Article 53 Where bidders collude with each other in bidding or collude with the tenderer in bidding, or where a bidder seeks to win the bid by bribing the tenderer or members of the bid evaluation committee, the award shall be invalid, and a fine of not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the amount of the winning project shall be imposed; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be fined not less than five percent and not more than ten percent of the fine imposed on the unit; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall also be confiscated; if the circumstances are serious, the bidder's qualification to participate in projects for which tender is required by law shall be revoked for a period of one to two years and such revocation shall be announced, and finally the business license may be revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law. If losses are caused to others, compensation liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 54 Where a bidder submits a bid in the name of another person or practices fraud by other means to obtain the award by deception, the award shall be invalid; if losses are caused to the tenderer, the bidder shall bear compensation liability according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Where a bidder in a project for which tender is required by law commits the acts listed in the preceding paragraph but does not constitute a crime, a fine of not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the amount of the winning project shall be imposed; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be fined not less than five percent and not more than ten percent of the fine imposed on the unit; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall also be confiscated; if the circumstances are serious, the bidder's qualification to participate in projects for which tender is required by law shall be revoked for a period of one to three years and such revocation shall be announced, and finally the business license may be revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce.

Article 55 Where, in a project for which tender is required by law, the tenderer, in violation of this Law, negotiates with bidders on substantive matters such as the bid price and bid proposal, the tenderer shall be given a warning, and the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where the acts listed in the preceding paragraph affect the result of the award, the award shall be invalid.

Article 56 Where a member of the bid evaluation committee accepts property or other benefits from a bidder, or where a member of the bid evaluation committee or relevant staff participating in the evaluation discloses to others the evaluation and comparison of the bid documents, the recommendation of candidates for winning the bid, or other information related to the bid evaluation, the member or staff shall be given a warning, the property accepted shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 3,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan may also be imposed; the member of the bid evaluation committee who has committed the listed illegal acts shall be disqualified as a member of the bid evaluation committee and shall not participate in the bid evaluation of any project for which tender is required by law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 57 Where the tenderer determines the winning bidder from among candidates other than those recommended by the bid evaluation committee according to law, or where, in a project for which tender is required by law, the tenderer determines the winning bidder on its own after all bids have been rejected by the bid evaluation committee, the award shall be invalid, the tenderer shall be ordered to correct, and may be fined not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the amount of the winning project; the person directly in charge of the unit and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 58 Where the winning bidder transfers the winning project to others, breaks up the winning project and transfers it separately to others, or in violation of this Law subcontracts part of the main or critical work of the winning project to others, or where the subcontractor subcontracts again, the transfer or subcontract shall be invalid, and a fine of not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the amount of the transferred or subcontracted project shall be imposed; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall also be confiscated; the bidder may be ordered to suspend business for rectification; if the circumstances are serious, the business license shall be revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce.

Article 59 Where the tenderer and the winning bidder fail to enter into a contract in accordance with the tender documents and the bid documents of the winning bidder, or where they conclude an agreement that deviates from the substantive content of the contract, the parties shall be ordered to correct; a fine of not less than five-thousandths and not more than ten-thousandths of the amount of the winning project may be imposed.

Article 60 Where the winning bidder fails to perform the contract concluded with the tenderer, the performance bond shall not be returned; if the losses caused to the tenderer exceed the amount of the performance bond, the winning bidder shall also compensate for the excess; if no performance bond was provided, the winning bidder shall bear compensation liability for the losses of the tenderer.
Where the winning bidder fails to perform its obligations in accordance with the contract concluded with the tenderer, and if the circumstances are serious, the winning bidder's qualification to participate in projects for which tender is required by law for a period of two to five years shall be revoked and such revocation shall be announced, and finally the business license may be revoked by the administrative authority for industry and commerce.
Where performance of the contract is impossible due to force majeure, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall not apply.

Article 61 The administrative penalties prescribed in this Chapter shall be decided by the relevant administrative supervision department designated by the State Council, unless this Law has otherwise provided for the authority imposing such penalties.

Article 62 Where any entity violates the provisions of this Law by restricting or excluding legal persons or other organizations from outside the region or system from participating in tendering, designating a tender agency for the tenderer, compelling the tenderer to entrust a tender agency with handling tender matters, or interfering in tendering and bidding activities by other means, it shall be ordered to make corrections; the persons directly in charge of the entity and other persons directly responsible shall be given warnings, demerit records, or serious demerit records according to law, and if the circumstances are relatively serious, they shall be given demotions, removal from office, or expulsion according to law.
Where an individual commits the illegal act prescribed in the preceding paragraph by taking advantage of his or her position, the liability shall be pursued in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 63 Where a functionary of a State organ who, according to law, bears the duty of administrative supervision over tendering and bidding activities engages in fraudulent practices for personal gain, abuses his or her authority, or neglects his or her duties, if the act constitutes a crime, the criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, he or she shall be given an administrative sanction according to law.

Article 64 Where a project that must be tendered according to law violates the provisions of this Law and the bid award is invalid, a new successful bidder shall be re-determined from among the remaining bidders in accordance with the bid award conditions prescribed by this Law, or tendering shall be conducted anew in accordance with this Law.

Article 65 Where a bidder or any other interested party considers that the tendering and bidding activities do not conform to the relevant provisions of this Law, it shall have the right to raise an objection with the tenderer or to file a complaint with the relevant administrative supervision department according to law.

Article 66 For projects that involve State security, State secrets, emergency rescue and disaster relief, or fall under special circumstances such as using poverty alleviation funds to implement work-for-relief programs requiring the employment of migrant workers, and are unsuitable for tendering, tendering may not be conducted in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 67 Where a project using loans or aid funds from international organizations or foreign governments is to be tendered, if the lender or fund provider has different provisions on the specific conditions and procedures for tendering and bidding, those provisions may apply, except where such application would violate the social public interests of the People's Republic of China.
Article 68 This Law shall come into force on January 1, 2000.
